None of the three answers is correct. The maximum is at least 11, which rules out 3, 4 and 8.

**Why the usual collision rules allow more than 3.** Two assistants on one edge collide in the interior only if their positions match at a non-vertex point at the same time. Two assistants that leave the same vertex together, both moving the same direction, meet only at that start vertex when the faster one is ahead. Two permanent bouncers on one edge always collide, so each edge can host at most one permanent resident. Fast assistants can pass through an edge once, before the resident is there or at a time when the resident is not in its interior.

**Refuting Solution 1 (answer 3).** Take three bouncers on the three edges at O with speeds 2, 4, 8. Let the speed-16 assistant go O→(0,0,1)→(0,1,1)→(1,1,1) and then loop around the face y=1. Its only shared edge is O–(0,0,1), which it traverses in [0, 1/16] alongside the speed-8 bouncer, meeting only at O. So n = 4 is achievable.

**Refuting Solution 3 (answer 4).** The same scheme extends. Adding a speed-32 walker that goes O→(0,0,1)→(1,0,1) and bounces there, then a speed-64 walker that goes O→(1,0,0)→(1,0,1) and bounces on that edge, and so on, one can check edge by edge that each permanent resident has its own edge and that every transit occurs either at the start from O or in a time window where the resident is absent. I checked this scheme through speed 2048 (n = 11) and found no interior collision. So 4 is too small.

**Refuting Solution 2 (answer 8).** The same construction already gives n = 11 with all 12 cube edges used or shared by transits, so 8 is too small.

I did not prove an upper bound, so I cannot state the exact maximum, but it is not 3, 4 or 8.

CHOICE: NONE
